articleTitle: Hybrid ARIMA and GRNN Model for Accurate Short-Term Water Level Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: To more effectively predict water levels, a hybrid method combining time-series analysis and artificial neural networks was proposed. The water level time series were sampled at regular intervals and forecast using the Auto-regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model. The results from the ARIMA model were then utilized as inputs for the Generalized Regression Neural Network (GRNN) to conduct accurate forecasting. The forecasting results demonstrate that this hybrid model can effectively predict short-term water level trends with stable prediction capability and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Compatibility-Based Recommendation Method for Ceramic Pattern Matching
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Ceramic culture is an important component of traditional Chinese culture, and its inheritance and innovation hold significant importance. As an essential carrier of ceramic art, ceramic patterns embody rich cultural symbolism and aesthetic value. To address the challenge of quantitatively matching user requirements with decoration combinations in ceramic design, this study proposes a compatibility-based recommendation method for ceramic decoration combinations. The method takes user-provided symbolic meanings and preferred elements as inputs. First, we integrate multi-dimensional information such as decorative elements and cultural symbolism to construct a knowledge graph. Second, we design a compatibility calculation model. The model combines shortest-path-based similarity measurement and overlapping community detection to quantify the compatibility potential between decorative elements. Finally, we propose a recommendation algorithm to recommend element combinations. These combinations satisfy users’ symbolic requirements while maximizing compatibility. Experimental results demonstrate that the method effectively enhances the coordination and cultural relevance of decoration combinations. This study provides an intelligent recommendation tool for ceramic decoration design. It can support the inheritance and innovation of ceramic culture.

articleTitle: Insurance Risk Factors Based on New Energy Vehicle Monitoring Big Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In recent years, new energy vehicle (NEV) industry in China has developed rapidly, but NEV insurance is facing the challenge of losses. The performance of power battery is an important factor affecting the safe operation of NEVs. Based on the monitoring big data of NEVs and utilizing the stability of charging data, state of healthy (SOH) calculation model, cell voltage consistency analysis model and module temperature consistency analysis model were established. Using the above power battery parameters, NEV insurance risk factor assessment model was established. The model in this work was tested using a ride hailing vehicle operating in Tianjin, and the test results showed that the risk factors relating to SOH, voltage consistency and temperature consistency were all at a high level, indicating a low probability of risk for the vehicle. The results can be used as a reference for insurance companies underwriting.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Feature Intelligent Prenatal Fetal Monitoring Algorithm Based on the PSO-RF Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In prenatal fetal state monitoring, fetal heart rate and uterine contraction data serve as important assessment criteria, yet they face data classification challenges. This paper proposes the PSO-RF algorithm, aiming to improve the prediction accuracy of prenatal fetal monitoring. By using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to automatically search for the optimal hyperparameter combination, the complexity of manual hyperparameter tuning is avoided. Meanwhile, the SMOTE oversampling technique is applied to balance the dataset, reducing the impact of data imbalance on model performance. The Isolation Forest algorithm is used to remove anomalous samples, improving data quality. The results indicate that compared to traditional models, the PSO-RF model shows a 2.2% improvement in precision, a 0.2% increase in accuracy, a 1.4% improvement in recall, and a 0.9% increase in the F1 score, especially demonstrating higher classification accuracy and lower computational overhead on imbalanced datasets. This method effectively enhances the performance of Random Forest (RF) on complex datasets. However, there is still room for further optimization in feature selection and applications involving large-scale datasets. Future research could combine other optimization methods and deep learning techniques to further enhance model accuracy and efficiency, and explore its potential applications in other fields.

Author Keywords: fetal heart rate and uterine contraction

articleTitle: Prediction Model for Minimum Miscibility Pressure in CO2-Oil Based on Automated Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: As a key means of improving oil recovery, the application effect of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flooding technology is restricted by many factors, the effectiveness of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flooding technology is restricted by many factors, with the minimum miscibility pressure (MMP) required to achieve the miscible phase of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-crude oil being the most critical parameter for determining oil displacement efficiency. In this study, the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-oil MMP prediction model was established using automatic machine learning, and the MMP was predicted and the results were analyzed. The results demonstrate that automatic machine learning can simplify the model development process through automatic model selection, hyperparameter optimization, and model fusion, significantly improving the prediction performance and accuracy of the model while accurately predicting the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-oil MMP. By comparing the predicted values of the model with the results of the slim tube experiment, the error was found to be within 5 %, indicating that the automatic machine learning model can effectively predict the MMP in Bayan Oilfield, providing valuable guidance for the development of CO2 flooding in oilfields.

articleTitle: MC-YOLO: A Context Aware Down Sampling Algorithm for Construction Site Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Safety accidents at construction sites not only pose a threat to the lives of workers but also lead to significant economic losses. Therefore, strengthening safety management at construction sites has become an issue that urgently needs to be addressed. Traditional construction site safety relies on manual inspection methods with low efficiency. Computer vision makes it possible to conduct automatic target detection in construction site. However, the complexity of the construction site environment and the diversity of detection targets pose challenges to detection. This paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 model called MC-YOLO for object detection in construction site. To overcome the problem of information loss caused by down-sampling in YOLOv8, a CADS (Content Aware Down-Sampling) block is proposed to replace the original down-sampling block. Meanwhile, in order to enhance the multi-scale object detection ability of YOLOv8, an improved C2f block named C2f-MSC (C2f with Multi-Scale Convolution) block is introduced. The addition of these two blocks not only improves the model’s feature extraction ability but also significantly reduces the number of model parameters. The experimental results show that the MC-YOLO model performs well on the CSS and SODA datasets. Specifically, The MC-YOLOs model achieves a mAP@0.5 of 80.8% and a precision of 91.9%, which are 1.5% and 3.9% higher than the original algorithm respectively, and the number of model parameters is reduced by 21.09%.

articleTitle: Learning From Category-attribute Label for Image Attribute Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In the field of image recognition, semantic attribute feature information of images plays a crucial role in enabling deep learning models to extract more comprehensive insights from the images. This allows the model to perform tasks such as fine-grained classification, zero-shot learning, and even model interpretability. However, compared to classification tasks that only require a single label, obtaining multiple semantic labels for images is often challenging. In the framework of weakly-supervised learning, partial-label learning allows models to learn a true label from multiple candidate labels. Relying on this learning paradigm, we propose Category-Attribute Labels Learning (CAL) based on the partial labels learning problem and corresponding learning algorithm to solve CAL problem. Category-attribute labels can be directly derived from textual descriptions of a category's attributes, which enable models to learn the true semantic features of images from low-cost attribute labels. In this paper, the category-attribute label problem has been formalized and shows through experiments that the model can effectively learn using category-attribute-labels. Our approach outperforms other state-of-the-art partial-label learning methods in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Accurate Brain Tumor Segmentation Based on an Improved U-Net with Feature Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Recently, image segmentation methods with high accuracy have become increasingly important in the diagnosis and treatment of brain tumors. Since segmentation models based on the U-Net architecture often have limited sizes for the sensing fields of image features, the contextual information thus cannot be fully used for segmentation. This paper proposes a new model that can effectively fuse multi-scale image features for the segmentation of brain tumor images. Firstly, an improved convolution module is utilized to replace the original convolutional component for the extraction of image features, which increases the depth and width of the network, and enhances its feature learning ability in complex tasks. Secondly, several improved downsampling and upsampling modules that have an inverted bottleneck structure with residuals are introduced in the sampling process, which maintains the semantic richness across various scales. Finally, a feature aggregation attention module is included in the bottom of the U-shape, which enables the network to pay more attention to effective regions and suppresses the noise. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves excellent segmentation performance on the brain tumor dataset BraTS 2021, and the Dice coefficients of whole tumor, tumor core, and enhancing tumor are 0.923, 0.890, and 0.861 respectively, which are improved by 1.6%, 1.3%, and 2.2% compared to the base network of the U-Net architecture. The proposed model can achieve an average value of 0.891 for the Dice coefficients and an average value of 5.172 for the Hausdorff distances. The results of comparison suggest that the proposed approach can outperform a few other state-of-the-art approaches for brain tumor segmentation.

articleTitle: DSnet: Removing scattered light in biomedical images using a Dual Stream neural network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Light scattering is a common phenomenon in biomedical imaging. However, its removal is a challenging task because of the complex light paths from the scattered light. In this paper, we propose a dual-stream neural network to computationally remove the scattered light in biomedical images. To achieve this task, we first derive a mathematical model from the classical dehazing model for natural images. Then, we propose a dual-stream neural network to solve this model. Different from the dehazing task for natural images that have clear images as ground truth, biomedical images usually do not have the ground truth. Therefore, we use images from two different modalities to train the dual-stream network without knowing the ground truth. Several experiments confirm that our method can significantly reduce the light scattering and improve the image quality. The proposed method can be applied in various applications where removing the scattered light is needed or preferred.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Learning based Image Denoising: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Image denoising is a fundamental yet challenging problem in the field of low-level vision tasks, as it directly affects the quality and usability of images in various applications. Over the years, numerous methods have been proposed to address this issue, with deep-learning based methods achieving particularly impressive performance. However, the robustness of these deep learning-based image denoising techniques is a crucial aspect that cannot be overlooked. Differences between testing and training conditions can significantly impact their performance in real-world scenarios, making it essential to develop methods that are both effective and adaptable. In recent years, many researchers have dedicated their efforts to improving the shortcomings of deep image denoising methods. Despite this, there has been a lack of systematic analysis and benchmarking of these methods, making it difficult to compare and evaluate their performance. To address this issue, we have conducted a comprehensive review of several deep learning-based image denoising methods which are all for natural images and classified them into four categories based on their different settings. For each category, we have selected representative methods and conducted benchmarking experiments using a public dataset, evaluating their performance both quantitatively and qualitatively. Through our experiments, we have observed some interesting trends and patterns in the performance of these methods. Based on our findings, we have provided detailed discussions and conclusions, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of each method and offering insights into future research directions. Overall, this paper contributes to the advancement of image denoising techniques by providing a systematic review and benchmarking of existing methods.

articleTitle: Transient Pulse Signal Recognition and Extraction in Particle Accelerator Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Particle accelerator devices belong to complex high-tech large scientific engineering equipment, and the electromagnetic environment is exceptionally complicated. Transient pulse signals negatively impact the operation of equipment in particle accelerator devices through conduction emission, cable crosstalk, near-field coupling, and other means. Therefore, identifying transient pulse signals in particle accelerator devices is an important topic for alleviating electromagnetic compatibility issues in particle accelerators. This paper systematically analyzes the causes and main effects of transient pulse signals generated by particle accelerator devices and proposes a transient pulse signal identification algorithm based on the threshold method. First, a testing system is constructed based on the IEC-61000-4-4 standard to obtain the pulse signal spectrum; second, a graphical pixel processing method is used to denoise the test spectrum; finally, based on the threshold identification algorithm, transient pulses are extracted, and the accuracy of different thresholds in signal identification is compared using the signal-to-noise ratio to define the optimal threshold, providing support for interference signal identification and spectrum management in particle accelerator devices.

articleTitle: CiteSpace-based Visualization and Analysis of Support Vector Machines in the Direction of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The purpose of this review is to provide an in-depth bibliometric analysis of Support Vector Machine (SVM) research literature in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in the Web of Science (WOS) database using the CiteSpace visualization tool. Since its introduction in the early 1990s, SVM has become one of the most important and widely used algorithms in the field of machine learning, especially in the fields of image recognition, bioinformatics, financial risk assessment and natural language processing. This paper reveals the trend of publication volume, major research institutions, hot topics and potential academic frontiers of SVM in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning through CiteSpace analysis. In the future, SVM research will evolve deeply while focusing on improving the explanatory power, trustworthiness, and transparency of the models, as well as safeguarding privacy and data security in their design and deployment. This review provides academics with a comprehensive overview of the research progress of SVM in the field of artificial intelligence and machine learning, provides references and insights for subsequent research, and provides data support and decision-making references for the teaching reform of related courses in colleges and universities.

articleTitle: Self-Geometric priors and rough-to-fine cascade optimization based on SSM for surface reconstruction from sparse point cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In the past few decades, we have greatly improved our ability to process point cloud data with the development of deep learning. Surface reconstruction has made significant progress, but there are still some challenges, such as meshes generated with holes, sensitivity to noise, and many approaches being hard to produce desirable results when faced with a wide variety of unseen classes. We designed the framework to be able to generate watertight meshes from the point cloud based on self-geometric priors and Mamba from rough to fine. First, we utilize a module based on adaptive graph convolution to upsample the point cloud for enhanced geometric information, subsequently, we employ a straightforward algorithm to swiftly generate a rough initial mesh. Following this, the self-geometric priors deform module, utilizing Mamba, is trained to iteratively adjust the vertex positions of the initial mesh. Eventually, a high-precision watertight mesh that conforms to the geometry of the point cloud is generated. We conducted a large number of experiments, and finally proved the effectiveness of each module of our framework, and improved the accuracy of point cloud reconstruction compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Elevator Based on Adaptive Transfer Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The early fault diagnosis of elevators is crucial for passenger safety and the riding experience. If a fault occurs but is not detected in time, it may lead to serious accidents. However, with a wide variety of elevator specifications and models, and highly variable operating conditions, constructing a generalizable diagnostic model presents a significant challenge. Moreover, obtaining labeled fault data is difficult, which greatly increases the complexity of early fault diagnosis and poses a challenge to ensuring the safe operation of elevators. To address this issue, a novel adaptive transfer network model for elevator fault diagnosis is proposed. The model is designed to process vibration data during elevator operation, thereby achieving better adaptation to equipment and working condition domains under conditions of label scarcity and sample imbalance. The model extracts and fuses rich vibration signal features from multiple sensors.. Additionally, cross-attention based on the exchange of classification information at different scales is designed to complement multi-scale fault features between the two branches. Finally, through fine-tuning of the model parameters, fault classification of target domain samples is achieved.

articleTitle: Research for Japanese Input Method using Flick in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In recent years, methods for displaying one’s own hands in virtual reality (VR) environments have been established through HMD (Head Mounted Display) equipped with hand-tracking features, such as the Meta Quest. However, currently, the speed and accuracy of text input using hand tracking in VR cannot be considered high. Therefore, this research aimed to reduce hand fatigue and improve speed and accuracy by combining hand tracking with flick input using a numeric keypad layout similar to that of smartphones. In this research, we developed a system that displays a numeric keypad layout keyboard in a VR space, allowing users to directly touch it and input text using flick gestures. The key layout is based on the numeric keypad commonly used for Japanese input on smartphones. It was conducted comparison experiment for text input using hand tracking in VR. The proposed method involved using flick input and pinch gestures, while the existing method used the standard hand tracking input method on Meta Quest. As a result, the proposed method received evaluations comparable to the existing system. The usability survey received an above-average rating and was evaluated as a good interface.

articleTitle: A small-sample bearing fault diagnosis method based on interpretable component energy features
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Due to the weak fault signals of motor bearings and the extreme difficulty in obtaining sufficient data samples, the requirements for training fault diagnosis models cannot be met. Moreover, current machine learning-based fault diagnosis methods lack interpretability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a small-sample bearing fault diagnosis method based on interpretable component energy features (ICEF). By combining the component energy values of bearing vibration signal samples with interpretable artificial intelligence techniques, an interpretable feature selection method is proposed. This method extracts effective features of bearing faults as training features for the fault diagnosis model, enhancing the model's ability to learn and identify fault category characteristics. Finally, experiments demonstrate that the fault diagnosis accuracy reaches 99.5% and 97.5% when component energy is used as the learning feature. Moreover, by mixing data from two bearing datasets and dividing them into training and test sets at different ratios, an accuracy of 91.7% is achieved, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method under small-sample conditions.

articleTitle: Gated Fusion based Multi Scale Feature Network for Landmark detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Architectures derived from the U-Net framework and its convolutional neural network (CNN) variants have garnered significant attention in computer vision due to their remarkable achievements. However, these methods predominantly focus on leveraging high-resolution low-level features for pixel-wise tasks such as semantic segmentation. Consequently, they fail to fully exploit global features and deep semantic information, resulting in insufficient localization of target regions and diminished performance in tasks requiring both global and local feature integration. In contrast, transformer-based frameworks have demonstrated superior efficacy in high-level semantic tasks. To address these limitations, a Multi-Scale Feature Network (MSFNet) is proposed, which is a novel cross-connected architecture integrating U-Net and Transformer, with multi-scale semantic feature learning being emphasized.

articleTitle: A Flexible Model for Predicting Workloads of Massive Microservices
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Deploying microservices into containers allows for dynamic adjustment of the resources required by each microservice based on predicted future workload. Typically, a cluster hosts a large number of different microservices. Due to frequent scheduling, most microservice containers have a short lifespan. Microservice workload prediction can help resource management. Microservice poses a challenge to workload prediction: how to flexibly predict massive short microservice workloads. In this paper, we propose a prediction model, DKM, which generates the Dynamic Kernel for each microservice, so as to flexibly predict massive diverse microservice workloads. DKM can learn from massive microservice workloads to build its own Kernel Dictionary, allowing it to generate the Dynamic Kernel for different microservices by selecting appropriate kernels from the dictionary. Experiments demonstrate that DKM performs well in workload prediction.

articleTitle: Demand Prediction with Gravity Graph Attention Networks for Shared Bike Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Shared bicycles, as an important component of green transportation, have experienced rapid development worldwide, making accurate demand forecasting crucial for urban transportation planning and operational management. However, existing deep learning approaches primarily focus on time series data and often fail to capture the complex spatial characteristics among stations. To address this issue, we propose a demand prediction method that integrates Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Gravity model. By constructing a geographic adjacency graph and incorporating multi-source information— such as station flow, built environment features, and geographic coordinates—into the node representations, the proposed method effectively combines the prior knowledge of the gravity model with the deep feature extraction capabilities of GAT, thus providing a comprehensive characterization of spatial interactions among stations. Experiments on a public dataset from Xiamen demonstrate that the fusion model outperforms standalone GAT, Gravity model, and GCN (Graph Convolutional Network) in terms of MAE, RMSE and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, validating its effectiveness and superiority in predicting shared bicycle demand.

articleTitle: Lightweight Voiceprint Recognition with Ghost Convolution and Hierarchical Residual Splitting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In the context of rapid development in digitization and the Internet of Things, voiceprint recognition has emerged as a secure, convenient, and cost-effective method for identity verification. Given the resource constraints of edge devices, designing a lightweight voiceprint recognition model is of great theoretical and practical significance. In this paper, following an initial evaluation of several mainstream models, the Efficient Channel Attention, Propagation and Aggregation Temporal Difference Neural Network (ECAPA-TDNN) is chosen as the baseline model for further enhancement. At the outset, both the SE-Res2Block and the Fully Connected Layer of the ECAPA-TDNN are enhanced utilizing the ghost convolution approach, with the objective of reducing computational cost and improving recognition performance. Building upon the innovation, the ECAPA-TDNN is further enhanced by integrating hierarchical residual splitting. Validation conducted on the CN-Celeb1 and AIShell-1 datasets demonstrates that the algorithm achieves significant reductions in parameter size and the number of floating-point operations, with only a minor reduction in accuracy. Consequently, the optimized algorithm is particularly suitable for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.

articleTitle: Core Loss Prediction Using a PC-GBT Model Based on Permutation Feature Importance and Grid Search Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: This study aims to predict core loss in magnetic materials using a PC-GBT model based on Permutation Feature Importance and Grid Search Optimization. The research analyzes the impact of three key factors—temperature, excitation waveform, and core material—on core loss, including both their individual and paired interactive effects, and evaluates the significance of each factor. Descriptive statistical analysis, distribution characteristics analysis, and univariate analysis were conducted to establish the relationships between core loss and these factors. The results indicate a positive correlation between core loss and both excitation waveform and material, while a negative correlation is observed with temperature. A two-factor analysis further explores the synergistic effects of temperature, material, and excitation waveform on core loss. Additionally, flux density data was extracted, and potential features were identified with reference to the core loss separation model and two modified Steinmetz equations. Benchmark model comparisons reveal that the Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT) model outperforms Support Vector Machines (SVM) in terms of prediction accuracy and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values. The development of the PC-GBT model includes Permutation Feature Importance analysis and Grid Search Optimization to identify the optimal hyperparameter configuration. Ultimately, the PC-GBT model demonstrates a lower mean error and an improved R2 value compared to the GBT model, confirming the effectiveness of the PC-GBT model.

articleTitle: PINN based short-term glucose prediction for type 1 diabetes
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Establishing a high-precision blood glucose prediction model is crucial for diabetes treatment and blood glucose management. Both physics-driven and data-driven models offer distinct advantages. Integrating information from both approaches is an effective strategy to enhance prediction accuracy and reduce computational expense. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) can incorporate physical information into neural networks, representing an emerging method for integrating physics and data. This study is the first to apply the PINN method to blood glucose prediction. Initially, a physiological model of blood glucose metabolism is established based on the principles of glucose metabolism. Subsequently, a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) structure is designed to establish the mapping relationship between blood glucose levels and the time series of food intake and insulin administration. Building upon this, a penalty function for training the RNN is designed, which includes the physical penalty term and network penalty term. Finally, the proposed method is experimentally validated on the 30 in-silico subjects with type 1 diabetes, derived from the FDA-certified UVa/Padova Simulator. The model achieves a 30-minute blood glucose prediction accuracy of 0.27 mmol/L.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Method Based on Hybrid Cuckoo Search and Firefly Algorithm for Breast Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: This research focuses on developing an efficient feature selection process using a hybrid technique combining Cuckoo Search algorithm and Firefly Algorithm. The Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset is utilized to evaluate the capability of selecting significant features and eliminating irrelevant ones. The experimental results demonstrate that using the hybrid technique significantly improves the accuracy of machine learning compared to using the Cuckoo Search and Firefly Algorithm individually. Additionally, an analysis was conducted on the impact of splitting the dataset for training and testing, with splits of 70/30, 80/20, and 90/10. The experiments revealed a relationship between the number of selected features and the model accuracy. The findings from this study can serve as a guideline for developing appropriate feature selection process for complex data analysis problems.

articleTitle: Knowledge Tracing Based on Memory Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Knowledge tracing aims to infer students’ mastery states of knowledge concepts through their interactive behaviors during learning, enabling personalized education systems to adaptively recommend materials. While existing models have improved predictive performance, their designs overlook core principles of human memory mechanisms. Learning and memory are intertwined cognitive processes: learning involves knowledge acquisition and integration, while memory controls information storage and retrieval. To address this gap, this study proposed a Knowledge Tracing Based on Memory Mechanism (MMKT) that analyzes interaction data by integrating the forgetting curve theory and spaced repetition theory. The model identifies three critical factors influencing memory retention strength: repeated time gap (time between consecutive interactions on the same concept), sequence time gap (time elapsed since the last interaction), and past trial counts (cumulative historical attempts). These factors are embedded into a dynamic key-value memory network, where a static key matrix encodes knowledge concepts and a dynamic value matrix updates mastery levels. An erase gate and an add gate are designed to control memory decay and consolidation, respectively. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that MMKT outperforms baseline models in accuracy (ACC) and area under the curve (AUC), demonstrating the effectiveness of memory mechanism modeling for enhancing knowledge tracing model performance.

articleTitle: Low-light Image Enhancement Network Based on Multi-Scale Dual-Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to improve the visual perception quality of low-quality images captured under insufficient lighting conditions and enhance the performance of downstream computer vision tasks. Due to the complex degradation factors in low-light images, it is difficult for most previous deep learning-based methods to learn the complex mapping relationship between low-light images and normal images by the single-scale learning mechanisms. Moreover, feature learning in the spatial domain is easily affected by noise signals, making it difficult to simultaneously restore brightness, color, and contrast. To solve these problems, we propose a multi-scale dual-domain low-light image enhancement network (MDENet). The network consists of an encoder-decoder structure, introducing a spatial-frequency dual-domain parallel feature learning architecture in the multi-scale recovery process. By adjusting local features in the spatial domain and employing Fourier transform for global information modulation in the frequency domain, a better image recovery mapping relationship is constructed. For the fusion of the obtained multi-scale recovery features, we propose an adaptive feature fusion module based on soft attention to achieve adaptive fusion of different input information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed MDENet outperforms the state-of-the-art methods quantitively and qualitatively. On LOL and LOL-v2 datasets, PSNR is 0.91 and 3.4 higher than the suboptimal method, and SSIM is 0.008 and 0.03 higher than the suboptimal method. The source code of this work will be released on GitHub.

articleTitle: Fine-grained Infectious Disease Surveillance Data Aggregation Scheme in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In the cloud computing environment, a fine-grained infectious disease monitoring data aggregation scheme is crucial for formulating effective epidemic prevention and control strategies. Developing a powerful data aggregation scheme for infectious disease monitoring requires careful consideration of several factors, including data integrity, fine-grained analysis, privacy protection, and fault tolerance. However, existing data aggregation schemes often fail to simultaneously address all of these issues. To address these challenges, we propose a cloud computing-based fine-grained infectious disease monitoring data aggregation scheme, which combines an improved Paillier encryption algorithm with Keyed-hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) and superincreasing sequences. This approach not only addresses the concerns mentioned above, but also enhances resilience against malicious data mining attacks. Meanwhile, the proposed scheme satisfies the desired security properties of the infectious disease surveillance system.

articleTitle: DMPNet: Robust Real-Time Intraoperative Parathyroid Identification via Novel Dual-Modality Fusion Framework of White-Light and Spectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Accurate intraoperative identification of parathyroid glands is crucial for preserving their function and min-imizing complications, such as hypocalcemia, during thyroid surgery. However, the small size, variable anatomical locations, and visual similarity of parathyroid glands to surrounding tissues make their identification challenging and heavily reliant on the surgeon’s expertise. To address these challenges, we propose DMPNet, a real-time dual-modality parathyroid detection framework that, for the first time, integrates white-light and spectral imaging for parathyroid detection. DMPNet is trained on a clinically relevant dataset comprising 3,309 white-light and 3,309 spectral images from 423 patients at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, reflecting diverse real-world surgical scenarios. The framework employs independent modality-specific feature extraction modules and a multi-scale fusion strategy to combine the complementary strengths of white-light and spectral imaging, significantly enhancing detection robustness and accuracy. The detection head processes these fused features, enabling precise localization and real-time identification of parathyroid glands. DMPNet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, with a precision of 0.887, recall of 0.749, and an F1-score of 0.764 on the test set—outperforming existing parathyroid detection models. With an impressive inference speed of 350.6 frames per second (FPS), far exceeding the standard endoscopic video frame rate of 25 FPS, DMPNet provides real-time assistance to surgeons, reducing cognitive burden, enhancing surgical precision, and minimizing postoperative complications. This pioneering integration of white-light and spectral imaging represents a significant advancement in intraoperative parathyroid gland identification, offering transformative potential for improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A Dual-Branch Brain Age Prediction Model Based on CNN and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Deep learning is used to accurately predict brain age based on neuroimaging data, especially brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) profiles. In previous studies, brain age prediction models were usually built using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract local features from images. However, the performance of CNNs is limited in modeling global information and long-distance dependencies which can be characterized by Vision Transformer (ViT). To address these challenges, we propose an innovative CNN-ViT dual-branch brain age prediction model. This model combines the strengths of both CNN and ViT, where the CNN branch extracts local features, and the ViT branch models global information using its powerful self-attention mechanism. We train the CNN-ViT dual-branch model to predict brain age using 10 public brain T1-weighted MRI datasets (N = 4310; age range: 18-95, years). By conducting a series of comparative and ablation experiments, the results show excellent prediction accuracy and the lowest predict error in validation set (N = 252; age range: 18-85, years), with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.77 years and a Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient (r) of 0.971. Additionally, we apply the CNN-ViT brain-age prediction architecture to predict the age of the whole brain and each brain region in a mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and a dementia dataset. We find the predicted brain age is significantly higher than the chronological age in both MCI and dementia patients. Furthermore, the brain age is older in dementia patients than that in MCI at the neurodegenerative neurodegeneration-prone regions. In conclusion, the CNN-ViT dual-branch architecture can effectively estimate the accelerated brain aging, which could assist in predicting neurodegeneration prognosis.

articleTitle: Real-time Multi-Object Tracking Algorithm for UAV Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with multi-target tracking technology are of significant importance in various key areas, including the management of modern urban life and military strategic deployment. This paper proposes an advanced Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) method with the combination of TStsm-yolov10 and an improved version of ByteTrack, which is well-suited to real-time multi-target tracking tasks for UAVs. In the realm of object detection, this paper introduces a tiny detection head to replace the existing large detection head, aiming to enhance the detection capabilities for small objects while constraining the parameter count. In the neck section, utilizing an improved TFPN for feature fusion across three distinct scales aims to improve the overall feature representation capability. Additionally, the SCSA attention mechanism has been integrated into the C2f module, designated as C2f-SCSA. The newly designed small object detection model is named TStsm-yolov10. For UAVs tracking, this paper enhances the Kalman filter by incorporating an adaptive noise estimation method to alleviate the impact of detection results. Experiments conducted on the VisDrone2019 dataset demonstrate that the improved methodology improves the detection performance, with a 5.7%, 5.6%, and 6.9% improvement in precision, recall, and mAP50, respectively. In terms of tracking performance, experiments on VisDrone2019-MOT-test and VisDrone2019-MOT-train demonstrated excellent tracking performance of the proposed method, with HOTA, MOTA and IDF1 improvements of 4.083% and 4.013%, 3.205% and 5.001%, and 5.221% and 5.988%, respectively. Furthermore, in comparison with the current popular two-stage tracking algorithms such as StrongSort and OCSort, the proposed method not only demonstrates excellent performance but also ensures real-time performance.

articleTitle: Document-Level Relation Extraction Based on Distant Supervision for Spring Water Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Document-Level Relation Extraction (DocRE) is essential for information extraction and knowledge graph construction. However, relation extraction in the spring water domain faces challenges such as data scarcity, noisy distant supervision, and difficulty in modeling cross-sentence relations. To address these issues, we propose a DocRE method integrating evidence sentence supervision and dynamic data denoising. We construct a distant supervision dataset, apply uncertainty estimation to filter noisy pseudo-labels, and enhance long-distance dependency modeling with evidence sentence supervision. Experiments on the spring water dataset show that our method outperforms baselines by 1.14% in IgnF1 and 0.99% in F1, demonstrating its effectiveness. Ablation studies further validate the impact of our proposed modules. Our approach mitigates noise and improves relation extraction accuracy, making it well-suited for low-resource domains.

articleTitle: Vector Field Based Algorithm Design for Water Surface Target Spatial Orientation Relation Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Recent research in computer vision has focused on understanding the semantic features of images. To address the spatial orientation relations among water surface targets, which is a fundamental semantic feature, this paper proposes the water surface target spatial orientation vector field (WST-SOVF) algorithm for recognizing spatial orientation relations. The WST-SOVF algorithm encodes these relations into a deep convolutional neural network with two branches: The T-branch employs key-point estimation to classify the target categories, while the S-branch determines the spatial orientation relations between targets by constructing the spatial orientation vector field. A fusion module is also employed to integrates features from both branches to produce a comprehensive triple list of targets, their spatial relations, and confidence levels. Experiments on Huawei’s "Typical Surface/Underwater Target Recognition" dataset demonstrate the algorithm’s excellent performance.

articleTitle: Kernel Functions in CNNs: Enhancing Robustness to Image Noise
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various fields, particularly in image processing. However, the interference from imaging devices and external environments introduces unavoidable noise, leading to a degradation in image quality. This paper proposes a Kernel-based Convolutional Neural Network (K-CNN) to enhance CNN robustness against image noise by incorporating kernel functions into convolution operations. The proposed K-CNN utilizes different types of kernel functions to improve nonlinear feature extraction without increasing model complexity. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that K-CNN significantly outperforms standard CNNs in handling Salt-and-Pepper and Gaussian noise. The results highlight the potential of kernel-based convolution operations as an alternative approach for improving CNN robustness in real-world noisy environments.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Kinematic Detection of Centrifugal Pendulum Vibration Absorber
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Using patented non-contact measurement technology based on computer vision, the kinematic characteristics of centrifugal pendulum vibration absorbers (CPVA) are measured. Firstly, the code wheel for computer vision recognition is arranged on the rotor and pendulum. Next, use a high-speed camera to record the movement process of CPVA in the video. Subsequently, with the help of digital image processing technology, the real-time motion positions of code wheel were identified. Finally, by utilizing the temporal variations of these position coordinates, the motion state parameters of the rotor and pendulum were successfully measured and compared with theoretical values. The results indicate that the proposed non-contact measurement method based on computer vision exhibits extremely high accuracy. This method not only offers robust support for the examination of CPVA’s dynamic characteristics but also pioneers innovative avenues for research in similar fields.

articleTitle: Direct Application of QAOA Algorithm to PUBO Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Previously, the approach to solving the PUBO (multiple unconstrained binary optimization) was to transform it into the QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) via variable substitution. Variable substitution is bound to introduce new variables, and when using the QAOA algorithm for solution, it also implies that inevitably more controllable qubits are required. However, this paper will explore how to directly apply the QAOA algorithm to the PUBO problem without converting the PUBO to QUBO, thereby reducing the utilization of qubits.

articleTitle: Physical Domain Deception Strategy: Experimental Verification of Adversarial Attacks on Vehicle Targets
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: While digital-domain adversarial attacks against vehicle detection models have matured with diversified implementations, research on physical-domain adversarial attacks still faces critical challenges, including environmental complexity and poor attack robustness. This paper establishes a digital-physical collaborative validation framework to systematically conduct empirical studies on physical-domain adversarial attacks. The methodology follows a dual-phase approach: First, adversarial samples are meticulously designed in the digital domain, followed by comprehensive physical-domain testing under multi-dimensional complex conditions, simulating varied heights (1.05–1.55 m), camera angles (0–360°), diverse backgrounds (sandy terrain, grassy terrain, runway, and parking lot), and illumination intensities (indoor and outdoor environments). Notably, this study innovatively introduces comparative experiments with traditional smoke interference scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed intelligent adversarial samples achieve an over 30% higher average attack success rate in physical environments compared to conventional smoke-based interference methods. The successful implementation of effective attacks against vehicle detection systems in real-world scenarios not only enriches the practical applications of adversarial attacks but also demonstrates substantial innovation in attack methodology. This research provides critical insights for enhancing the robustness of autonomous driving systems while establishing new theoretical foundations for physical-domain adversarial attack studies. Furthermore, the findings suggest that future research should focus on developing more sophisticated defense mechanisms to counteract these advanced adversarial attacks, ensuring the safety and reliability of intelligent systems in complex real-world environments.

articleTitle: Hybrid compressed lightweight epilepsy detection network based on greedy strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Epilepsy is a disorder of abnormal discharges in the brain, which is sudden and may lead to death in severe cases. Tens of millions of patients suffer from it every year. EEG is an effective tool for recording brain electrical activity. However, manual observation of the EEG to diagnose whether a person has epilepsy is time-consuming and labour-intensive. Thus automated epilepsy testing by EEG has become popular in recent years. In this paper, we propose a brief and efficient lightweight inverted triangular seizure detection network (LITEDN), which takes 1D channel-selected electroencephalogram (EEG) signals as input. The baseline achieves an inference accuracy of 96.08%, with a sensitivity of 95.69%, a precision of 96.44%, a specificity of 96.46%, and an F1 score of 96.06%. Based on the baseline, filter pruning is applied. Result in a mere 1.3% loss in network accuracy while reducing the number of parameters by 96.78%. Finally, a hybrid compression algorithm based on greedy strategy is proposed to further compress the bit width on the basis of filter pruning. The number of network parameters after hybrid compression is only 7.504 K, which is not only 124 times more compressed than LITEDN, but also the number of parameters in the epilepsy detection network after hybrid compression has reached a more advanced level in recent years.

articleTitle: Software Crowdsourcing Allocation Algorithm Based on Publisher Heterogeneous Service Expectations
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that reliable crowdsourcing workers in existing research are unstable in heterogeneous tasks, a software crowdsourcing assignment algorithm based on publishers’ heterogeneous service expectations (PHSE) is proposed. First, the efficiency and reputation scores of workers are calculated based on the explicit feedback of their historical behaviors. Then, candidate crowdsourcing workers are selected and their skills are scored based on the complexity and skill requirements of the tasks to be assigned. Finally, the optimal matching of crowdsourcing workers and tasks is achieved based on service expectations. Experimental results show that compared with the artificial bee colony algorithm based on skill matching, the ant colony algorithm based on efficiency indicators, the worker selection algorithm based on reputation indicators, the task assignment algorithm based on user reliability, and the task assignment algorithm based on grouping and reorganization, the task assignment success rate and task completion quality of the proposed algorithm are improved by an average of 1.98% and 32.27% respectively, which can effectively guide task assignment.

articleTitle: A Multi-layer Composite Radial Basis Neural Network Combined with PINN to Solve Partial Differential Equations
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: A novel approach for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) is introduced in this paper by integrating a multi-layer composite radial basis neural network (MCRBNN) with a physical information neural network (PINN). Initially, a multi-layer radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is constructed, and the optimal number of structural layers is determined. Subsequently, sub-networks are integrated into each layer to form a composite multi-layer RBFNN. Adjustable radial basis functions are used in each layer of subnetworks. To address the sensitivity of RBFNN to initial parameter values, particularly the center and width of the radial basis function, the last layer is augmented with a PINN. The performance and effectiveness of the method in PDEs are demonstrated through two numerical experiments. Moreover, its outstanding solution accuracy and speed are highlighted, even when the quantity of training samples remains unchanged in comparison with those of some existing methods.

articleTitle: Quantum Attack Implementation of TWINE Block Cipher
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The result of resource consumption in quantum attack implementation of cryptographic algorithm is an important metric to evaluate the security strength of cryptographic algorithm against quantum attack. This paper studies complete implementation of quantum attack on cryptographic algorithm using Grover meets Simon method. We find 9-round quantum distinguisher whose round is the longest currently about TWINE, and utilize Grover meets Simon method to carry out 14/15-round quantum key recovery attack on TWINE-80/TWINE-128 with lower complexity than exhaust attack. Furthermore, we give complete implementation of quantum oracle and QAA algorithm in TWINE’s quantum key recovery attack for the first time. The circuit is suitable for all implementation of quantum key recovery attack on block cipher using Grover meets Simon method.

articleTitle: IgnisGrowth: A Novel Combustion-Growth Inspired Method for Point Cloud Completion
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Point cloud completion is a key task in 3D point cloud processing, addressing the challenge of reconstructing the full shape of a 3D object from incomplete data. We propose a novel method, IgnisGrowth, which simulates a gradual "growth" process of the point cloud. Inspired by natural growth mechanisms, our method starts from local regions and expands to the global structure, recovering local details and ensuring global consistency. Extensive experiments show that IgnisGrowth outperforms existing methods on widely used benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/yizilaohan/IgnisGrowth.

articleTitle: A deep-learning-based method for pitch shifting and tone complement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Most instruments have an effective range of no more than four octaves, and with the Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) standard supporting up to 128 different pitches, it is necessary to expand the range of an instrument's timbre artificially. Experiments demonstrate that the time domain envelope and the frequency domain characteristics of the sample playback synthesized tones differ quite from the actual tones. Deep learning techniques have been widely used in timbre synthesis and music composition, but no one has applied them to pitch shifting and tone complement. This paper introduces the pitch deviation problem to CNN and RNN, and the time-domain similarity between synthetic pitch and actual pitch reaches 99.99%, more than 29% higher than the traditional method. It is found that high-frequency noise is present in the synthesized tones, so the synthesized audio is filtered using different orders of Butterworth low-pass filters (LPF). The results show that the first-order LPF gives the best results in both time and frequency domains, removing high-frequency noise. This method can be used in home-convenient medical devices that enable music therapy to save storage space for tones and enable tonal complementation.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Scientific Database Supporting In-situ Data Query and Accessing
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Scientific databases have become an increasingly popular and important asset in cloud computing, HPC, big data, and AI, which many applications rely on. The performance of querying on scientific databases is crucial as applications frequently select a specific subset of the database to work on based on certain attribute values. Current solutions support scientific databases by combining relational databases (RDB) and distributed file systems (DFS). However, in production environments, they usually cannot be collocated on the same cluster. To make matters worse, the production DFS’s dynamic namespace prevents the RDB from storing DFS file paths as the value. This results in remote file copying from the RDB server to the production DFS where computation programs load data, greatly limiting the system’s overall performance. To this end, this paper presents SEAFS, a file system that supports efficient searching on file extended attributes. First, SEAFS proposes an integrated indexed attribute storage scheme using a three-level search tree and weak link semantics to organize attributes directly within the file system namespace, enabling redundancy-free storage and rapid attribute searching. Second, SEAFS supports fuzzy searching with a per-attribute dedicated index using general suffix automata to provide optimized matching performance. Evaluations demonstrate that SEAFS outperforms the current solution (without remote copying) by 25.98–79.40× and 2.58–2271× in multi-threaded precise searching and fuzzy searching respectively.

articleTitle: Classification and prediction-based data mining algorithms to predict visitors to the museum
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The perception that museums are often perceived as disconnected from everyday life has resulted in a notable reluctance among a substantial segment of the population to visit these institutions. To enhance visitor attendance, it is essential to conduct an analysis of social survey databases. The objective of this study is to identify potential museum visitors within a given population and to predict their likelihood of visiting through the application of a data mining model utilizing classification algorithms. The dataset employed in this research was sourced from the "2021 China General Social Survey." We implemented five classification algorithms using the opensource software WEKA to classify and predict the dataset, specifically Naive Bayes, Logistic, J48, Random Trees, and KStar. Among these algorithms, the J48 classification method yielded the highest accuracy in predicting potential visitors, achieving a success rate of 78.7012%. The findings suggest that lifestyle habits and individual preferences play a significant role in determining the frequency of museum visits. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of classification and prediction algorithms in the context of museum visitor research and proposes several promising avenues for future investigation.

articleTitle: MCANet: A Multi-Scale Class-Related Attention Network for Few-Shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Among various few-shot learning methods, metric learning approaches based on local feature representation of images have achieved remarkable results. However, most of these methods coarsely compare support sets and query sets at a single scale, failing to consider the contextual information of image data and the diversity of multi-scale information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Multi-scale Class-related Attention Network for few-shot learning, referred to as MCANet. In MCANet, we first construct a multi-scale feature extraction module that adopts a bottom-up architecture to capture image features from multiple scales and levels, thereby combining high-level semantic representations with low-level visual information. The images are then represented as sets of local features at different scales. Next, we utilize data co-occurrence information to select class-related features for each category, highlighting semantically dominant objects at various scales while reducing the influence of irrelevant local features. Finally, we integrate contextual information to fuse similarity measures across different scales for comparing query and support sets. On the miniImageNet dataset, our MCANet achieves accuracies of 71.08% (5-way 1-shot) and 83.34% (5-way 5-shot), and demonstrates competitive performance on other popular benchmarks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method is effective for few-shot learning.

articleTitle: Knowledge Synergy Complement Learning for Multi-Skill Dialogue Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The field of multi-skill dialogue generation focuses on creating conversational agents capable of handling a variety of tasks. Traditional approaches, such as task detection and adapter fusion, have faced challenges; task detection heavily depends on accurate context recognition, while adapter fusion methods often suffer from high computational complexity and are constrained by the performance of single-adapter models. To address these issues, we propose a novel method called Knowledge Synergy Complement (KSC) learning for enhancing multi-skill dialogue generation. In KSC, we leverage single-skill adapters by defining their Lipschitz constants as macro knowledge and utilizing intermediate hidden states to capture micro knowledge. This complementary approach allows for better integration of diverse skills. Moreover, a novel knowledge pruning mechanism is introduced to prevent knowledge forgetting and reduce conflict between skills. Our experiments demonstrate that KSC effectively integrates multiple skills, achieving superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods, while also being more efficient in terms of computational and storage resources required.

articleTitle: A new method of contrastive clustering based on fuzzy soft labels
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel contrastive clustering method based on fuzzy labels (FLC) to address the limitations of existing clustering methods in selecting and utilizing positive samples. Traditional methods often rely on hard positive samples and nearest-neighbor relationships, which can lead to robustness issues and inaccurate cluster assignments. FLC enhances feature representation learning by leveraging both hard and soft positive samples, representing classes as fuzzy sets to calculate the grade of membership for each target sample. This allows for the construction of robust soft positive samples. We introduce a weighted soft contrastive loss that incorporates these grades of membership, guiding the learning process to focus on significant instances for accurate class representation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and STL-10 datasets demonstrate that FLC outperforms traditional and deep clustering methods, achieving significant improvements in clustering accuracy (ACC), normalized mutual information (NMI), and adjusted rand index (ARI). Ablation studies confirm the contributions of each component, with the combined use resulting in substantial performance gains. Parameter analysis further shows that increasing the number of label samples per class enhances clustering performance, with optimal results achieved around ten samples. FLC effectively learns cluster-friendly feature representations, proving its robustness and effectiveness in unsupervised image clustering.

articleTitle: A genetic-based convolutional neural networks optimization for fault diagnosis of rotary agriculture machine
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are an effective and accurate method for vibration analysis in fault detection. However, optimizing hyper-parameters and network topology is a time-consuming task. This paper focuses on two main points. First, it demonstrates that CNN architecture can be automatically optimized using a genetic algorithm (GA) to achieve the desired accuracy. Second, it tests these optimized CNNs for fault detection in rotary agriculture machines using vibration analysis, an ongoing challenge in the field. The methodology includes the population of various CNNs with the architecture optimized by GA for the spectrographic representation of vibration signals. Two most common faults were considered: 1) lack of oil in the main shift, and 2) broken tooth in the rotor. The results show that CNNs with GA optimization predict the lack of oil in the shift with 99% accuracy, whereas the broken tooth in the rotor was detected with 100% accuracy. The best results were obtained using metrics vector with MLP and SVM. The mean accuracy across 100 iterations was 0.995.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Prediction of Mixed-Precision Quantization for Edge Model by Graph Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) technology has significantly increased the demand for edge models deployed on edge devices. However, the computational, storage, and energy limitations of these devices necessitate the efficient optimization and compression of models. Mixed-precision quantization (MQ) has emerged as an effective technique for reducing resource consumption while preserving model performance. Despite its potential, accurately and efficiently evaluating the performance loss due to quantization during the deployment phase remains a significant challenge. Traditional evaluation methods are often time-consuming and computationally expensive. To address this, we first construct an enhanced mixed-precision quantization model dataset, MQ-Bench-201, and then design an MQ evaluator using graph neural network (GNN) techniques. This evaluator is capable of accurately predicting performance loss across different quantization configurations of neural architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed evaluator outperforms existing architecture encoding-based predictors, both on the MQ-Bench-201 dataset and in terms of generalization to other datasets. The source code and dataset is released in: https://github.com/Leannnnnnn/MQ-Bench-201.

articleTitle: Improved Magic Square Transform Combined with Double Random Phase Encoding for Iris Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: To address the issue of iris template leakage using irreversible transformation, this study proposes a new double iris template protection method that combines an improved magic square transformation with Double Random Phase Encoding (DRPE). Firstly, the user's iris features using the log-Gabor transform were extracted, then scrambling iterations and transformation matrix parameters. The iris feature matrix is divided into non-overlapping blocks and scrambled for the first layer of encryption protection using the improved magic square method. Next, in the fractional Fourier transform domain, DRPE is applied to construct an encrypted feature vector. This involves using a user-defined mask M1 and a second mask M2 derived from the user’s other iris image, for a second layer of encryption on the scrambled matrix. Finally, encrypted templates are matched for recognition using Hamming distance. Images from the CASIA-IrisV3-Interval, MMU-V1, and CASIA-IrisV4-Lamp iris databases were used to test the algorithm's performance. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 98.93%, can generate a total of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup> possible templates, and requires 314<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">52×624</sup> ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup> attempts to recover the original data. This approach meets the standards for irreversibility, revocability, and unlinkability in biometric template protection.

articleTitle: Textured Surface Defect Detection with Image-Level Accuracy Optimization via Patch-Level Features and Simulation-Based Samples
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Textured surface defect detection plays a critical role in industrial product quality monitoring. However, excessive reliance on pixel-level precision, especially when defect boundaries are unclear, can lead to more complex models, lower efficiency, and increased risk of false positives or missed detections, ultimately compromising system reliability. Additionally, challenges such as the difficulty of collecting defect samples, severe class imbalances, and high pixel-level labeling costs hinder the effectiveness of convolutional neural networks in terms of both inference speed and computational efficiency. To overcome these challenges, we propose SiamSimNet, a dual-channel Siamese network that relies on high-quality training data generated through simulation algorithms, minimizing the need for real defect samples. By incorporating locally aware patch features, the proposed method significantly improves detection accuracy and robustness, while maintaining high inference efficiency. This approach shows strong potential for real-world industrial applications.

articleTitle: TransformBioRegressor: A Transformer-based Grassland Biomass Estimator using Multi-source Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Accurately monitoring aboveground biomass (AGB) in grassland ecosystems is critical for sustainable grassland management and ecological protection. In this paper, TransformBioRegressor is proposed for estimating AGB by utilizing multi-source data, including remote sensing, geographic, and meteorological data. It is a transformer-based model that integrates self-attention mechanisms with multi-layer perceptron (MLP) structures. Extensive experiments have shown that TransformBioRegressor consistently outperforms other models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, and MLP, in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Rsquared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). TransformBioRegressor achieves an RMSE of 59.47 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, a MAPE of 27.85%, and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.80 when using full spectral bands. Additionally, this study analyzes the spatial and temporal distribution of AGB in West Ujimqin Banner, a representative grassland region in northern China, and identifies precipitation as the most significant environmental factor influencing biomass, further enhancing the understanding of grassland dynamics.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamic Programming Control for Robust Disturbance Rejection and Error Minimization in Dynamic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Dynamic programming (DP) and reinforcement learning (RL) are effective techniques for maximizing control in uncertain and dynamic systems. In order to improve decision-making in control applications, this study combines RL and DP with an emphasis on error minimization and disturbance rejection. The strategy in the RL framework aims to maximize expected returns and is organized as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). The method allows for enhanced adaptive control techniques, error minimization, and disturbance rejection by integrating state and action value functions. In order to maximize system performance, the study also investigates dynamic control equations using the Bellman principle and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman formulations. The suggested approach improves overall system stability by increasing tracking speed, reducing control errors, and fortifying robustness against sudden disturbance.

articleTitle: Rumor Suppression Maximization Algorithm Based on Local Dominance Tree
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: With the advancement of computer technology and the convenience of information dissemination, online social networks have become a significant platform for the spread of various types of negative information. Rumors, as a prominent form of negative information on social media, can cause social unrest and lead to economic losses. Therefore, how to quickly and effectively curb the spread of rumors has become a key issue in current social network research. Based on the Independent Cascade Model, combined with graph sampling techniques and the Three Degrees of Influence principle, an improved rumor suppression maximization algorithm, RSM-LDT , is proposed. Firstly, considering the role of deep network node structures in influence diffusion, a local dominance tree is defined to calculate the potential influence of nodes. Secondly, based on the Independent Cascade Model, the node with the highest potential influence is selected as the blocking node each time. The effectiveness of the RSM-LDT algorithm is verified by comparing its rumor suppression effect and running time with five existing algorithms on two publicly available real datasets. Experimental results show that the blocking seed set selected by the RSM-LDT algorithm proposed in this paper is more accurate, significantly reducing the spread of rumors compared to heuristic algorithms, and the running time of the algorithm is four orders of magnitude faster than that of greedy algorithms. The RSM-LDT algorithm can solve the problem of rumor suppression maximization in social networks, avoiding the high time complexity of greedy algorithms while addressing the poor suppression effect of heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: CD-DVC: Conditional Diffusion Model for Distributed Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2025 4th Asia Conference on Algorithms, Computing and Machine Learning (CACML)
abstract: Conventional predictive coding-based video compression techniques encounter notable difficulties when deployed on wireless terminal devices with constrained computational capabilities, primarily due to their dependence on resource-intensive encoders. Distributed Video Coding (DVC) alleviates this issue by transferring the computational load from the encoder to the decoder. However, traditional DVC methods still fall short in performance when compared to predictive coding strategies. Drawing inspiration from the impressive advancements of deep learning in image and video compression, we introduce CD-DVC, an innovative end-to-end DVC framework. CD-DVC adheres to the independent encoding and joint decoding paradigm of DVC, enabling efficient compression of Wyner-Ziv (WZ) frames. At the encoder, a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) is employed to compress WZ frames into low-dimensional latent representations. At the decoder, a conditional diffusion model is introduced to guide the progressive denoising of a pure noise image, leveraging the latent representation of the WZ frame and the information from decoded Key frames to reconstruct high-quality WZ frames. Experimental results demonstrate that CD-DVC outperforms the traditional VVC/H.266 intra standard and the current deep learning (DL)-based end-to-end distributed video coding scheme, LDVC [1], in terms of reconstruction quality. This work provides a new solution for video compression in resource-constrained wireless environments.
